script:
[measured] Ek simple sawaal se shuru karte hain. Do plus do kitna hota hai? Aapke dimaag mein turant answer aaya — "chaar." Koi effort nahi laga. Ab dusra sawaal — sattaais guna chauttees kitna hota hai? Yahaan aapka dimaag ruk gaya. Calculation shuru hui. Effort lага.

[instructive] Yehi do experiences — Daniel Kahneman ki kitaab "Thinking, Fast and Slow" ka core hain. Ek Nobel Prize winning psychologist, jisne humein sikhaya ki hum sochte kaise hain — aur zyada important, hum galat kaise sochte hain, bina jaane.

[pause]

[serious] Kahneman kehte hain — humare dimaag mein do systems kaam karte hain. System 1 aur System 2.

[instructive] System 1 — fast, automatic, emotional. Ye bina soche react karta hai. Jab aap kisi ke face pe anger dekhte hain, turant samajh jaate hain. Jab aap gaadi chalate hain familiar road pe, aapko concentrate nahi karna padta. Ye System 1 hai.

System 2 — slow, deliberate, logical. Jab aap tax calculate karte hain, jab aap kisi mushkil decision pe soch rahe hote hain, jab aap naye rasty pe parking kar rahe hote hain — ye System 2 activate hota hai.

[measured] Problem ye hai ki System 2 lazy hota hai. Wo energy bachana chahta hai. Toh zyadatar decisions — System 1 lete hain. Fast, automatic, aur — bahut baar — galat.

[pause]

[serious] Yahin se shuru hota hai humara pehla core idea — cognitive biases. Mental shortcuts jo humein galat direction mein le jaate hain, bina humein pata chale.

[instructive] Pehla bias — Anchoring Effect. Kahneman ne experiment kiya. Logo ko ek wheel spin karne diya gaya, jisme number aata tha — bilkul random, one se hundred tak. Fir unse poocha gaya — "Africa mein United Nations ke kitne countries hain?" Jinke wheel pe bada number aaya tha, unhone bada guess diya. Jinke chhota number aaya, unhone chhota guess diya.

[measured] Random number ka koi connection nahi tha sawaal se. Phir bhi usne answer ko anchor kar diya.

[reflective] Sochiye — jab aap kisi showroom mein jaate hain, aur salesman ek expensive product pehle dikhata hai, phir cheaper option — wo cheaper option achha lagta hai. Kyun? Kyunki pehla number aapke dimaag mein anchor ban chuka hai. Negotiation mein, salary discussion mein, real estate mein — pehla number jo table pe aata hai, wahi baaki sab kuch decide karta hai.

[serious] Ye humari decision-making ki sabse badi kamzori hai — hum sochte hain hum logically decide kar rahe hain. Lekin asal mein, ek invisible anchor humein pehle se control kar chuka hota hai.

[pause]

[instructive] Doosra bias — Availability Heuristic. Iska matlab hai — jo cheez jitni aasaani se yaad aati hai, hum usko utna hi common ya likely samajhte hain.

[measured] Kahneman ka example lete hain. Poochiye kisi se — "English mein 'K' letter se shuru hone wale zyada words hain, ya jisme third letter 'K' ho, wo zyada hain?" Zyadatar log kahenge — pehle wale, kyunki unhe yaad karna aasan hai. Lekin reality mein, third letter wale words zyada hain.

[reflective] Yahi wajah hai ki plane crash ke baad log flying se darne lagte hain — jabki car accident se marne ka chance kahin zyada hota hai. Kyun? Kyunki plane crash news mein zyada dikhta hai. Wo memory mein "available" hai. Aur available cheezein humein "likely" lagti hain — chahe wo statistically sach na ho.

[serious] Yaad rakhiye — jo dikhta hai, wo hamesha sach nahi hota. Jo yaad rehta hai, wo hamesha common nahi hota. Ye distinction samajhna — mental toughness ki pehli seedhi hai.

[pause]

[authoritative] Ab teesra aur sabse powerful idea — Loss Aversion.

[instructive] Kahneman aur unke partner Amos Tversky ne discover kiya ki insaan ke liye — kuch khona, kuch paane se zyada dard deta hai. Exactly double.

[measured] Matlab — agar aapko hundred rupees milne ka chance hai, aur hundred rupees khone ka bhi chance hai — dono equal probability pe — toh bhi aap risk nahi lenge. Kyunki loss ka dard, gain ki khushi se psychologically bada feel hota hai.

[reflective] Isi wajah se log bura stock hold karke rakhte hain, loss book nahi karte — kyunki "loss accept karna" emotionally itna mushkil hota hai. Isi wajah se log bekar relationship mein rehte hain, bekar job mein rehte hain — kyunki chhodne ka "loss" unhe rokta hai, chahe growth kahin aur ho.

[serious] Ye samajhna zaroori hai — hum rational nahi hain. Hum loss se bachne ke liye design kiye gaye hain — chahe wo bachna humein aage badhne se rok de.

[pause]

[authoritative] Aur ek concept jo Kahneman deta hai — jo shayad sabse zyada practical hai — Overconfidence aur "What You See Is All There Is."

[instructive] Humara dimaag stories banata hai. Jab bhi koi outcome hota hai — success ya failure — hum turant ek explanation bana lete hain. "Wo successful hua kyunki wo disciplined tha." "Wo fail hua kyunki wo lazy tha."

[measured] Lekin Kahneman kehte hain — hum information ki completeness check nahi karte. Jo bhi limited data available hai, hum uske basis pe confident conclusion bana lete hain. Chahe wo data adhoora ho, chahe usme luck ka bada role ho.

[reflective] Isi wajah se hum successful logon ki biography padh ke sochte hain — "Bas ye formula follow karo, safal ho jaoge." Lekin hum unn hazaaron logon ki kahaniyan nahi padhte, jinhone wahi formula follow kiya — aur fail ho gaye. Survivorship bias. Hum sirf winners dekhte hain, aur unse universal rule bana lete hain.

[serious] Kahneman kehte hain — confidence, accuracy ka proof nahi hai. Kayi baar sabse confident insaan sabse galat hota hai — kyunki uska System 1 usse ek smooth, convincing story bata raha hota hai. Aur smooth story hamesha true nahi hoti.

[pause]

[authoritative] Toh in sab ideas se hum kya seekhte hain?

[instructive] Pehla — apne fast decisions pe blind trust mat kijiye. Jab bhi koi important decision aaye — financial, career, relationship — apne System 2 ko jaga kar rakhiye. Turant react mat kijiye. Ruko, socho, phir bolo.

[measured] Doosra — apne biases ko identify karna seekhiye. Anchoring, availability, loss aversion — ye sab automatically chalte hain. Aap inhe completely khatam nahi kar sakte. Lekin aap inhe pehchan sakte hain. Aur jab aap pehchante hain, tab hi aap control le sakte hain.

[reflective] Teesra — confidence ko intelligence mat samjhiye. Duniya mein sabse loud voice hamesha sabse sahi voice nahi hoti. Aur khud ki confidence bhi — hamesha verify kijiye data se, emotion se nahi.

[pause]

[serious] Kahneman ki poori kitaab ka essence yahi hai — humara dimaag do tarah se kaam karta hai. Ek fast, automatic, aur bahut baar galat. Doosra slow, effortful, lekin zyada accurate.

[authoritative] Discipline ka matlab yahi hai — apne fast dimaag ko pehchanna, aur zaroorat padne pe apne slow dimaag ko activate karna. Har waqt System 2 use nahi kar sakte — energy khatam ho jayegi. Lekin important decisions ke liye — career, paisa, health, relationships — wahan System 2 ko jagana zaroori hai.

[reflective] Sochiye — kitni baar aapne koi decision liya sirf isliye kyunki wo "achha laga," "sahi feel hua"? Aur kitni baar us decision ka result baad mein regret bana?

[pause]

[serious] Ye kitaab humein ye nahi sikhati ki hum perfect ban jaayein. Ye sikhati hai ki hum aware ban jaayein. Awareness hi pehla step hai control ka.

[measured] Jab aap jaante hain ki aapka dimaag anchor pe react karta hai, aap dusri baar us anchor ko question karenge. Jab aap jaante hain ki available memory hamesha truth nahi hoti, aap data dhoondhenge, feeling nahi. Jab aap jaante hain ki loss ka dard aapko galat decision mein phasa sakta hai, aap ek step peeche jaake sochenge.

[authoritative] Yahi hai real mental toughness — apne hi dimaag se ek healthy distance banaye rakhna. Uspe blind trust na karna. Har fast thought ko ek baar slow soch se test karna.

[pause]

[serious] Kahneman ne apni zindagi is field mein di — humein ye samjhane ke liye ki hum jitna sochte hain ki hum rational hain, utne hain nahi. Lekin is truth ko accept karna hi hume behtar decisions lene ki taraf le jaata hai.

[reflective] Toh agli baar jab koi bada decision saamne aaye — ruko. System 1 ko bolne do, lekin final faisla System 2 ko lene do.

[authoritative] Kyunki jo apne dimaag ko samajhta hai, wahi apni zindagi ko control karta hai. Baaki sab — sirf reaction mein jeete hain.
